occupation: Pedlar, then glazier and painter in New York City; land proprietor at Brattleboro

events.title: Pedlar's licence
events.description: Paid GBP 5 for a one-year licence to trade as a pedlar (receipt signed A. De Peyster). [R4-S1]

events.title: Marriage
events.description: Married his first wife Mary Conkling. [R4-S1]

events.title: Brattleboro declaration
events.description: First signer of a declaration that the people of the town were loyal to the State of New York (the Vermont jurisdiction dispute), not Tories. [R4-S1]

bio: Second son of Henry Wells I (b. 1690), grandson of William Wells II and Elizabeth Tuthill (Hayes, [R4-S1]). He is John's 2nd cousin 9 times removed through William Wells and again through John Tuthill (1635). He left Southold at about 18, peddled under a 1735 New York licence, became a glazier and painter (also selling lottery tickets in 1749), joined the purchase of a large tract at Brattleboro, and died at Montague aged 83 years 6 months.
sources: [R4-S1] Charles W. Hayes, William Wells of Southold and his Descendants (1878) (archive.org full text), ch. VI (secondary) https://archive.org/details/williamwellsofso00byuhaye
